results.content:
Tuesday’s The Economist/YouGov poll came only a day after the president got less-than-stellar news from the newest Reuters/Ipsos poll released Aug. 24.

For the second week in a row, the poll found Trump’s approval rating sitting at 33%, the lowest approval rating the president has seen in Reuters/Ipsos tracking since his return to the White House in 2025. The numbers also tie Trump’s worst approval rating during his first term in office, in December 2017. [...] Despite the president’s improvement in The Economist/YouGov’s tracking in recent weeks, Trump is still hovering within 3 percentage points of his lowest approval rating since his return to the White House in 2025 (33%).

results.title: Trump approval rating still hovering near record lows, new poll shows

results.content:
In the latest Economist/YouGov survey, Trump is exiting August with a 33 percent approval rating, a new low for him in that poll.

Trump’s polling in the Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) average did see a slight increase Thursday, reaching 39.2 percent.

Still, this average marked the second-lowest released by DDHQ since May, when Trump averaged 38 percent. The polling average also found that 57.5 percent disapproved of the president.
results.title: Trump’s approval ratings endure a cruel summer

results.content:
An Economist/YouGov poll released Aug. 11 found that 33% of Americans approve of Trump’s job performance, a 3-percentage-point drop from the previous week, reported USA TODAY. The latest figure marks Trump’s lowest approval rating in YouGov polling since he returned to the White House in 2025. [...] The economy continues to weigh on Trump’s approval numbers, as it has in several recent polls. The Economist/YouGov poll found that just 22% of Americans rate the economy as excellent or good, while only 14% say economic conditions are improving.

Meanwhile, more than half of Americans — 56% — believe the economy is getting worse.

The Economist/YouGov poll was conducted Aug. 7-10 among 1,589 U.S
